docs.title: Home
docs.text: Welcome to the home of the Open Pattern Format documentation. Here you will find everything you need relating to the Open Pattern Format whether you are a yarn crafter, designer or developer.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Open Pattern Format or OPAF for short is a comprehensive file format specification for digital yarn craft patterns and projects. The specification covers all elements which make up your average pattern including metadata, components, instructions and charts.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Structured metadata
  • Configurable & customisable
  • Standardised terminology
  • Interactive instructions & charts
  • Project tracking
  • XML based (can be read in any text editor)
  • Free, open source & permissive

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Open Pattern Format supports a set of basic functions which can be used throughout a pattern for things like conditions and values. The functions are designed to align with those found in many spreadsheet packages to make it easy to translate formulas direct from grading sheets.

docs.title: ABS
docs.text:
ABS returns the absolute value of a number. The absolute value of a number is the number without its sign.

Syntax

ABS(val)

  • val: The value to process (required)
Example Result ABS(-1) 1 ABS(1) 1

docs.title: AND
docs.text:
AND returns true if all test conditions are true.

Syntax

AND(cond1, cond2)

  • cond1: The first condition to test (required)
  • cond2: The second condition to test (required)
Example Result AND('true', 'true') true AND('true', 'false') false AND(EQ(1, 1), GT(10, 1)) true AND(EQ(1, 2), GT(10, 1)) false

docs.title: BOOL
docs.text:
BOOL converts values of different types to a boolean value.

This function is useful for converting strings such as yes and no to a boolean value for a condition.

Strings "true", "yes" and "1" will return true. Strings are converted to lower case before evaluation.

Values of 1 will return true, anything else will return false.

Syntax

BOOL(val)

  • val: The value to process (required)
Example Result BOOL(1) true BOOL(22) false BOOL('No') false BOOL('yes') true BOOL('true') true BOOL('true') false

docs.title: CEIL
docs.text:
CEIL returns a number rounded up to the desired multiple.

Syntax

CEIL(val, multiple)

  • val: The value to round up (required)
  • multiple: The multiple to round up to (default: 1)
Example Result CEIL(3.7, 2) 4 CEIL(4.2) 5 CEIL(9, 4) 12 CEIL(1.22, 0.2) 1.4

docs.title: CHOOSE
docs.text:
CHOOSE returns a given value based on an index.

This is useful for returning a value such as stich count based on size.

Index starts at 1.

Syntax

CHOOSE(index, values)

  • index: The index of the desired value (required)
  • values: An array of values in the form [0,1,2,3] (required)
Example Result CHOOSE(2, [5, 6, 7, 8]) 6 CHOOSE(4, ['true', 'true', 'false', 'true']) true

docs.title: EQ
docs.text:
EQ tests whether one value is equal to another.

A single value or an array of values in the form [0,1,2,3] can be provided to test against.

All strings will be converted to lower case before comparison so doing case sensitive comparisons is not possible.

Syntax

EQ(val, test)

  • val: The value to test (required)
  • test: The value or values to test against (required)
Example Result EQ(1, 24) false EQ(-1, -1) true EQ(23, [21,22,23,24]) true EQ(1, [0,2,4,5]) false EQ('Test', 'test') true

docs.title: FLOOR
docs.text:
FLOOR returns a number rounded down to the desired multiple.

Syntax

FLOOR(val, multiple)

  • val: The value to round down (required)
  • multiple: The multiple to round down to (default: 1)
Example Result FLOOR(3.7, 2) 2 FLOOR(4.8) 4 FLOOR(9, 2) 8

docs.title: GT
docs.text:
GT returns whether one number is greater than another.

Syntax

GT(val, test)

  • val: The value to test (required)
  • test: The value to test against (required)
Example Result GT(3.7, 5) false GT(5, 2) true

docs.title: IF
docs.text:
IF returns the specified value based on a given condition.

Syntax

IF(condition, valueT, valueF)

  • condition: The test condition (required)
  • valueT: Value to return if condition is true (required)
  • valueF: Value to return if condition is false (required)
Example Result IF(true, 1, 2) 1 IF(false, 1, 2) 2 IF(EQ(1, 2), 1.3, 2.5) 2.5

docs.title: ISEMPTY
docs.text:
ISEMPTY returns whether a variable exists or contains no value.

This function is useful for testing non-mandatory configuration values such as custom lengths so you know whether a custom value has been provided or a default value should be used.

Syntax

ISEMPTY(val)

  • val: The value to test (required)
Example Result ISEMPTY('') true ISEMPTY('stuff') false

docs.title: LT
docs.text:
LT returns whether one number is less than another.

Syntax

LT(val, test)

  • val: The value to test (required)
  • test: The value to test against (required)
Example Result LT(3.7, 5) true LT(5, 2) false

docs.title: MAX
docs.text:
MAX returns the largest value from those provided.

Syntax

MAX(val1, val2)

  • val1: The first value to compare (required)
  • val2: The second value to compare (required)
Example Result MAX(3, 5) 5 MAX(5.4, 5.6) 5.6 MAX(-2, 3) 3

docs.title: MIN
docs.text:
MIN returns the smallest value from those provided.

Syntax

MIN(val1, val2)

  • val1: The first value to compare (required)
  • val2: The second value to compare (required)
Example Result MIN(3, 5) 3 MIN(5.4, 5.6) 5.4 MIN(-2, 3) -2

docs.title: MOD
docs.text:
MOD returns the remainder after a value is divided by a divisor.

Syntax

MOD(val, div)

  • val: The value for which you want to determine the remainder (required)
  • div: The number to divide the value by to find the remainder (required)
Example Result MOD(3, 2) 1 MOD(3, -2) -1 MOD(20, 5) 0

docs.title: MROUND
docs.text:
MROUND returns a number rounded to the desired multiple.

Syntax

MROUND(val, multiple)

  • val: The value to round (required)
  • multiple: The multiple to round to (default: 1)
Example Result MROUND(1.456) 1 MROUND(62, 8) 64 MROUND(1.3, 0.2) 1.4 MROUND(10, 3) 9

docs.title: MULTIPLE
docs.text:
MULTIPLE returns whether a value is a multiple of a given number.

0 is a multiple of all numbers.

Syntax

MULTIPLE(val, multiple)

  • val: The value to test (required)
  • multiple: The multiple to test against (default: 1)
Example Result MULTIPLE(10, 0) true MULTIPLE(30, 10) true MULTIPLE(30, 4) false

docs.title: NEQ
docs.text:
NEQ tests whether one value is not equal to another.

A single value or an array of values in the form [0,1,2,3] can be provided to test against.

All strings will be converted to lower case before comparison so doing case sensitive comparisons is not possible.

Syntax

NEQ(val, test)

  • val: The value to test (required)
  • test: The value or values to test against (required)
Example Result NEQ(1, 24) true NEQ(-1, -1) false NEQ(23, [21,22,23,24]) false NEQ(1, [0,2,4,5]) true NEQ('Test', 'test') false

docs.title: NOT
docs.text:
NOT returns the opposite of a given value so true becomes false.

Syntax

NOT(val)

  • val: The value to process (required)
Example Result NOT('true') false NOT('false') true NOT(EQ(1, 1)) false NOT(LT(10, 1)) true

docs.title: OR
docs.text:
OR returns true if any test conditions are true.

Syntax

OR(cond1, cond2)

  • cond1: The first condition to test (required)
  • cond2: The second condition to test (required)
Example Result OR('true', 'false') true OR('false', 'false') false OR(EQ(1, 3), GT(10, 1)) true

docs.title: ROUND
docs.text:
The ROUND function rounds a decimal value to the nearest whole number. It is useful for converting floating point values to integer after operations such as division.

Syntax

ROUND(val)

  • val: The value to round (required)
Example Result ROUND(1.456) 1 ROUND(1.5) 2 ROUND(2.7) 3

docs.title: Developer Documentation
docs.text:
Open Pattern Format is an XML based specification which can describe a yarn based pattern and project. Pattern files use XML macros to provide dynamic elements which can generate custom project files based on user preferences.

Open Pattern Format consists of two closely related specifications. One for describing a pattern and another for describing a project. A pattern file is used to generate a project file which can then be read by any compatible reader software. A pattern requires 'packaging' before it can be distributed which is a means of making a pattern self-contained with all images and other associated data.

docs.title: OPAF Pattern Specification
docs.text:
Pattern files have the extension .opaf and should be seen as source code for a given pattern. Pattern files require packaging before being distributed.

A pattern is built using the following basic elements:

  • <opaf:component>
  • <opaf:instruction>
  • <opaf:action>

docs.title: Pattern
docs.text:
A pattern file requires a <pattern> root element with the following attributes:

  • xmlns:opaf: "https://github.com/open-pattern-format/opaf"
  • name: The name of the pattern [required]
  • version: Version number which is compatible with the Symantic Versioning Specification (e.g. 1.0.0) [required]
  • unique_id: UUID identifier for the pattern (e.g. 89ab9835-10c0-46a8-89ab-d81b980a1d97)
Pattern Example
<pattern version="1.0.0" xmlns:opaf="https://github.com/open-pattern-format/opaf" name="My First Pattern" unique_id="123ab456-1234-56cc-d789-60f8305bcdab">

</pattern>

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
Metadata is indicated by a <opaf:metadata> node which will contain nested child elements. See the metadata specification documentation for more information.

Metadata Example
<opaf:metadata>
    ...
</opaf:metadata>

docs.title: Color
docs.text:
Colors which will be used in the pattern are defined using <opaf:define_color> nodes. The following attributes are supported:

  • name: A string identifier for the color. The name must not contain spaces.
  • description: A short description of the color and what it is used for.
  • value: A hex representation of the color or one of the following [black, silver, white, red, purple, green, yellow, blue]
Color Example
<opaf:define_color name="contrast" value="#2a365c" description="Contrast yarn"/>

docs.title: Action
docs.text:
Actions are used to build instructions in a pattern. Everything from a simple knit stitch to cables are defined using actions.

A set of standard knitting actions are defined HERE.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Open Pattern Format consists of three closely related specifications each with their own file type:

  • Pattern - .opaf files store the pattern source and will generally not be distributed by the designer in their raw form. A pattern in .opaf format requires packaging before it can be distributed.

  • Package - .opafpkg files are packaged, self-contained patterns which can be distributed by the designer. These files can be used to generate projects.

  • Project - .opafproj files are generated from packaged pattern files based on individual user configuration. An .opafproj file can be used with any compatible reader and is stand-alone so does not depend on the original pattern file. Project tracking is also integral.

docs.title: Pattern Creator Overview
docs.text: Pattern Creator is an application to help designers create OPAF patterns.

docs.title: Pattern Manager Overview
docs.text: Pattern Manager is an application for managing OPAF patterns and projects.
